headline: Investors and AI founders at San Francisco's Tech Week are pleased with the White House's hands-off approach to regulating AI, the AP reports.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: a mood report from one event that restates a known policy; the pact itself was covered on 30 Sep.
importance_line: Founders and investors back voluntary safety rules, which leave the public relying on companies to police themselves rather than on law, but this is a report from one event, not a measure of how the pact works.
summary: The Associated Press reports from Tech Week in San Francisco that venture capitalists and AI founders are pleased with the White House's stance on AI regulation, after President Trump signed a voluntary safety pact with tech leaders that, AP says, leaves AI labs to police themselves without detailed safety rules; our 30 Sep 2026 edition carried The Guardian's report of the signing at the White House on 29 Sep. AP adds that companies have disclosed their AI models' role in many troubling cyberattacks this year, yet the sector keeps driving economic growth, and that the US has lost ground on governing AI compared with a few years ago.
notes: AP's own site returned 403; the opening paragraphs were read on the Kokomo Tribune copy of the AP story and the summary stays inside them. The editor may wish to confirm the rest of the AP story if it becomes available.
